newsitem.title: HONG KONG: RESEARCH ALERT- HSBC rated accumulate.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT- HSBC rated accumulate.

text.p: Merrill Lynch has revised its earnings outlook for HSBC Holdings Plc upwards and says the bank is trading at a 20 percent discount to its revised fair value.

"HSBC's share price now stands at 80 percent of our esitmated fair value. We believe that long-term appreciation potential outweighs the possible risk of any near-term correction," Keith Irving said in a report dated May 14.
"We estimate fair value at HK$695 billion-HK$722 billion versus a current market capitalisation of HK$577 billion," the report said.
"In PER (price/earnings ratio) and price/book terms, HSBC still looks inexpensive versus both global and domestic competitors in its major markets."
The report also said a 20 percent discount may be too steep for the 'conglomerate', given HSBC is essentially in one business although it operates in many markets.
The listed bank's fundamentals remain sound with pre-exceptional earnings per share growth of 21 percent forecast in 1997 and 14 percent next year, the report said.

The forecasts are based on HSBC's advantages which enable it to service major corporates not only at head office level but also in most of the markets in which they operate and spread one technology research and development spend across all its retail banking networks, it said.

"The establishment of a significant Latin American retail business adds another leg to HSBC's growth story whilst the possibility of restructuring certain Asian business to provide better access to local markets cannot be entirely ruled out," it said.
